Supplied exact Confidence Protocol skill, verbatim:

---
name: confidence-protocol
description: Implement, fix, refactor, research, or review software with explicit proof obligations, proportional verification, and traceable evidence. Use when the user requests Confidence Protocol or justified confidence in a software change.
---

# Confidence Protocol

Deliver the requested outcome with evidence a teammate can inspect. Command success, current source, and sufficient proof are separate judgments.

## Establish the contract

Identify observable success, important regressions, constraints, and unresolved facts before implementation. Turn consequential claims into disprovable obligations. Trace the actual behavior through its execution and validation gates; a prerequisite that exists but is invalid must not enable an action or promise readiness.

Use the lightest adequate process: **Quick** for clear, reversible local edits; **Standard** for ordinary bugs, features, and implementation-guiding research; **Critical** for consequential trust, money, destructive data, migration, or broad product changes. Use [mode examples](references/modes.md) and [task profiles](references/task-profiles.md) when the proof scope needs clarification. Explain the proof plan briefly. Preserve scope and existing authorization; continue discovery, implementation, repair, and verification autonomously. Ask only for an unresolved consequential choice or an action requiring additional authorization. Finish authorized preparation before that decision.

## Build and challenge

Choose a small useful change that fits repository conventions. For bugs, reproduce the failure, then verify the fix. Exercise important boundaries through public behavior; mocks establish only the behavior they retain. If a claim depends on persistence or an external contract, run that boundary or mark the claim partial.

Use independent review for Critical work, consequential unresolved assumptions, changed trust/persistence/service contracts, surprising proof failures, or failures that are difficult to detect or undo. A reversible local mapping can use focused checks when it changes no such boundary; record why. Give the reviewer a narrow counterexample question and raw evidence. Critical work needs separate test-design and adversarial-review roles. Obtain independent proof design before implementation; review the resulting change adversarially afterward. Retain reviewer origin, scope, findings, and a resolvable reference; never invent independence. If required review is unavailable, disclose the gap. External model calls need authorization covering cost and data exposure.

Prefer one clear owner per rule, direct code, and abstractions justified by current needs. Remove unused scaffolding. Tests should have small readable setup, literal failure messages, and cases that could reject the claim. Avoid duplicated coverage and mocks that erase the boundary being tested.

## Verify and finish

Rerun affected proof after relevant code, test, or environment changes. Reuse current sufficient evidence; do not repeat passing checks solely for ceremony. Resolve failures before expanding the test scope.

For Standard/Critical repository work, read [evidence.md](references/evidence.md) for capture, incremental recording, and completion semantics. Keep read-only requests read-only unless artifact creation is authorized. Required missing proof stays partial; optional exclusions remain visible with reasons. Successful validation checks evidence rules, not the truth of every product claim.

Report delivered behavior, strongest relevant proof, remaining uncertainty, evidence location, and rollback when consequential. State exactly what was verified. Continue until the authorized outcome is delivered or a concrete blocker prevents further useful work.


Implement the requested behavior on this frozen historical base. Run visible checks and record actual uncertainty. No held-out tests or gold implementation are available. Supplied toolkit files are immutable under .protocol.

Fix coordinator event routing so a native child thread completing its turn cannot finish or replace the active coordinator turn. Only events belonging to the active coordinator thread/turn may establish its outcome. Preserve the coordinator final receipt and process cleanup behavior. For legacy notifications lacking threadId, a completion with the active turn ID remains accepted. Allowed production paths: bonaparte, bonaparte_native.py. New regular root *.py helper modules are allowed; do not shadow Python standard-library or test-framework modules.
This is an isolated repository snapshot with baseline tests. Keep testing offline; do not fetch history, accepted solutions or external services. Do not run live Bonaparte provider workflows. Use fixture patterns. An evaluator restores original tests and applies held-out checks to declared production files; added tests do not affect grading.



Common authorization: The user authorizes isolated local source edits, offline fixtures/tests, and fresh same-model support reviews within this shared cost/data envelope. No further permission is needed for those actions. No network, original history, other trial data, or hidden grading is authorized. Allowed production paths: ["bonaparte", "bonaparte_native.py"]; legitimate new ordinary root Python helpers may accompany the production change, but must not shadow stdlib/test framework names. Agent-written tests supplement visible proof; grading restores original tests. Place tests under tests/, proof packets under .confidence/, and disposable repro files under .trial-tmp/. Do not edit unrelated production paths or the injected AGENTS.md/.gitignore envelope.

Visible test commands:
[["python3", "-B", "-m", "unittest", "tests.test_phase_runtime"]]

At the end return the required JSON object. complete=true means the requested behavior and required proof are complete according to the supplied protocol and your observed visible evidence. List required gaps in remaining. This statement is collected independently of the hidden acceptance check; do not claim access to a hidden oracle. A successful protocol validation alone does not establish substantive software correctness.

description: Implement, fix, refactor, research, or review software with explicit proof obligations, proportional verification, and traceable evidence. Use when the user requests Confidence Protocol or justified confidence in a software change.

# Confidence Protocol

Deliver the requested outcome with evidence a teammate can inspect. Command success, current source, and sufficient proof are separate judgments.

## Establish the contract

Identify observable success, important regressions, constraints, and unresolved facts before implementation. Turn consequential claims into disprovable obligations. Trace the actual behavior through its execution and validation gates; a prerequisite that exists but is invalid must not enable an action or promise readiness.

For complex or long-running work, use [complex tasks](references/complex-tasks.md) to preserve dependencies, authority, blockers, review provenance, and recovery state. Use [harness guidance](references/harnesses.md) when delegating across Codex, Claude Code, or T3 Code. Resolve model and runtime capabilities from current documentation and actual receipts; a model name or agent count is not proof.

Use the lightest adequate process: **Quick** for clear, reversible local edits; **Standard** for ordinary bugs, features, and implementation-guiding research; **Critical** for consequential trust, money, destructive data, migration, or broad product changes. Use [mode examples](references/modes.md) and [task profiles](references/task-profiles.md) when the proof scope needs clarification. Explain the proof plan briefly. Preserve scope and existing authorization; continue discovery, implementation, repair, and verification autonomously. Ask only for an unresolved consequential choice or an action requiring additional authorization. Finish authorized preparation before that decision.

## Build and challenge

Choose a small useful change that fits repository conventions. For bugs, reproduce the failure, then verify the fix. Exercise important boundaries through public behavior; mocks establish only the behavior they retain. If a claim depends on persistence or an external contract, run that boundary or mark the claim partial.

Use independent review for Critical work, consequential unresolved assumptions, changed trust/persistence/service contracts, surprising proof failures, or failures that are difficult to detect or undo. A reversible local mapping can use focused checks when it changes no such boundary; record why. Give the reviewer a narrow counterexample question and raw evidence. Critical work needs separate test-design and adversarial-review roles. Obtain independent proof design before implementation; review the resulting change adversarially afterward. Retain reviewer origin, scope, findings, and a resolvable reference; never invent independence. If required review is unavailable, disclose the gap. External model calls need authorization covering cost and data exposure.

Prefer one clear owner per rule, direct code, and abstractions justified by current needs. Remove unused scaffolding. Tests should have small readable setup, literal failure messages, and cases that could reject the claim. Avoid duplicated coverage and mocks that erase the boundary being tested.

## Verify and finish

Rerun affected proof after relevant code, test, or environment changes. Reuse current sufficient evidence; do not repeat passing checks solely for ceremony. Resolve failures before expanding the test scope.

For Standard/Critical repository work, read [evidence.md](references/evidence.md) for capture, incremental recording, and completion semantics. Keep read-only requests read-only unless artifact creation is authorized. Required missing proof stays partial; optional exclusions remain visible with reasons. Successful validation checks evidence rules, not the truth of every product claim.

Report delivered behavior, strongest relevant proof, remaining uncertainty, evidence location, and rollback when consequential. State exactly what was verified. Continue until the authorized outcome is delivered or a concrete blocker prevents further useful work.


Implement the requested behavior on this frozen historical base. Run visible checks and record actual uncertainty. No held-out tests or gold implementation are available. Supplied toolkit files are immutable under .protocol.

Allow operators to disable the soft phase time budget explicitly, including on resume. Disabled budgets must wait for normal provider completion without sending budget steering. Persist the disabled choice in checkpoints. Preserve defaults and positive finite numeric budgets, and reject invalid inputs before invoking a provider. The public CLI flag is --no-soft-phase-budget; retain --soft-phase-budget-seconds for positive finite numbers. Null/None in a persisted soft_phase_budget_seconds field means disabled. run_phase(..., soft_phase_budget_seconds=None) must support disabled execution. BONAPARTE_SOFT_PHASE_BUDGET=off disables the default; a positive numeric --soft-phase-budget-seconds overrides that environment setting. The two CLI budget flags are mutually exclusive. Allowed production paths: bonaparte, bonaparte_checkpoint.py. New regular root *.py helper modules are allowed; do not shadow Python standard-library or test-framework modules.
This is an isolated repository snapshot with baseline tests. Keep testing offline; do not fetch history, accepted solutions or external services. Do not run live Bonaparte provider workflows. Use fixture patterns. An evaluator restores original tests and applies held-out checks to declared production files; added tests do not affect grading.

Apply the supplied Confidence Protocol with fresh scoped review. Use the common request_review tool for a narrow proof-design question before implementation and an adversarial counterexample question after the change, within the shared trial budget. Give reviewers the requirements, relevant source and raw visible evidence rather than a proposed verdict. Reconcile concrete findings against behavior, repair real defects and rerun affected proof. Preserve reviewer outputs and origin. Different context or reviewer agreement is not authenticated independence or product proof; unresolved required findings keep completion partial. Review capability is the same as in all other arms.

Common authorization: The user authorizes isolated local source edits, offline fixtures/tests, and fresh same-model support reviews within this shared cost/data envelope. No further permission is needed for those actions. No network, original history, other trial data, or hidden grading is authorized. Allowed production paths: ["bonaparte", "bonaparte_checkpoint.py"]; legitimate new ordinary root Python helpers may accompany the production change, but must not shadow stdlib/test framework names. Agent-written tests supplement visible proof; grading restores original tests. Place tests under tests/, proof packets under .confidence/, and disposable repro files under .trial-tmp/. Do not edit unrelated production paths or the injected AGENTS.md/.gitignore envelope.

# Confidence Protocol

Deliver the requested outcome with evidence a teammate can inspect. Command success, current source, and sufficient proof are separate judgments.

## Establish the contract

Identify observable success, important regressions, constraints, and unresolved facts before implementation. Turn consequential claims into disprovable obligations. Trace the actual behavior through its execution and validation gates; a prerequisite that exists but is invalid must not enable an action or promise readiness.

For complex or long-running work, use [complex tasks](references/complex-tasks.md) to preserve dependencies, authority, blockers, review provenance, and recovery state. Use [harness guidance](references/harnesses.md) when delegating across Codex, Claude Code, or T3 Code. Resolve model and runtime capabilities from current documentation and actual receipts; a model name or agent count is not proof.

Use the lightest adequate process: **Quick** for clear, reversible local edits; **Standard** for ordinary bugs, features, and implementation-guiding research; **Critical** for consequential trust, money, destructive data, migration, or broad product changes. Use [mode examples](references/modes.md) and [task profiles](references/task-profiles.md) when the proof scope needs clarification. Explain the proof plan briefly. Preserve scope and existing authorization; continue discovery, implementation, repair, and verification autonomously. Ask only for an unresolved consequential choice or an action requiring additional authorization. Finish authorized preparation before that decision.

## Build and challenge

Choose a small useful change that fits repository conventions. For bugs, reproduce the failure, then verify the fix. Exercise important boundaries through public behavior; mocks establish only the behavior they retain. If a claim depends on persistence or an external contract, run that boundary or mark the claim partial.

Use independent review for Critical work, consequential unresolved assumptions, changed trust/persistence/service contracts, surprising proof failures, or failures that are difficult to detect or undo. A reversible local mapping can use focused checks when it changes no such boundary; record why. Give the reviewer a narrow counterexample question and raw evidence. Critical work needs separate test-design and adversarial-review roles. Obtain independent proof design before implementation; review the resulting change adversarially afterward. Retain reviewer origin, scope, findings, and a resolvable reference; never invent independence. If required review is unavailable, disclose the gap. External model calls need authorization covering cost and data exposure.

Prefer one clear owner per rule, direct code, and abstractions justified by current needs. Remove unused scaffolding. Tests should have small readable setup, literal failure messages, and cases that could reject the claim. Avoid duplicated coverage and mocks that erase the boundary being tested.

## Verify and finish

Rerun affected proof after relevant code, test, or environment changes. Reuse current sufficient evidence; do not repeat passing checks solely for ceremony. Resolve failures before expanding the test scope.

For Standard/Critical repository work, read [evidence.md](references/evidence.md) for capture, incremental recording, and completion semantics. Keep read-only requests read-only unless artifact creation is authorized. Required missing proof stays partial; optional exclusions remain visible with reasons. Successful validation checks evidence rules, not the truth of every product claim.

Report delivered behavior, strongest relevant proof, remaining uncertainty, evidence location, and rollback when consequential. State exactly what was verified. Continue until the authorized outcome is delivered or a concrete blocker prevents further useful work.


Implement the requested behavior on this frozen historical base. Run visible checks and record actual uncertainty. No held-out tests or gold implementation are available. Supplied toolkit files are immutable under .protocol.

A soft time-budget interruption or post-steer guard failure after a native session exists must return a bounded failure receipt with a durable usable continuation token and saved question. Resuming that token must reuse the same native session. Bootstrap failures, ordinary protocol errors and session mismatches must not create misleading continuation checkpoints. Allowed production paths: bonaparte. New regular root *.py helper modules are allowed; do not shadow Python standard-library or test-framework modules.
This is an isolated repository snapshot with baseline tests. Keep testing offline; do not fetch history, accepted solutions or external services. Do not run live Bonaparte provider workflows. Use fixture patterns. An evaluator restores original tests and applies held-out checks to declared production files; added tests do not affect grading.

Apply the supplied Confidence Protocol by first proposing concrete inputs or execution paths that could disprove the requested behavior. Before editing, reproduce one relevant failure through available public behavior where feasible and state the important preserved behavior. Implement the smallest causal fix, then exercise the original counterexample and at least one consequential boundary or preservation control. Treat unexplained passing output and reviewer agreement as insufficient. If reproduction is unavailable, record that gap and use the strongest available check without inventing a failure.

Common authorization: The user authorizes isolated local source edits, offline fixtures/tests, and fresh same-model support reviews within this shared cost/data envelope. No further permission is needed for those actions. No network, original history, other trial data, or hidden grading is authorized. Allowed production paths: ["bonaparte"]; legitimate new ordinary root Python helpers may accompany the production change, but must not shadow stdlib/test framework names. Agent-written tests supplement visible proof; grading restores original tests. Place tests under tests/, proof packets under .confidence/, and disposable repro files under .trial-tmp/. Do not edit unrelated production paths or the injected AGENTS.md/.gitignore envelope.

Visible test commands:
[["python3", "-B", "-m", "unittest", "tests.test_bonaparte"]]

At the end return the required JSON object. complete=true means the requested behavior and required proof are complete according to the supplied protocol and your observed visible evidence. List required gaps in remaining. This statement is collected independently of the hidden acceptance check; do not claim access to a hidden oracle. A successful protocol validation alone does not establish substantive software correctness.

# Confidence Protocol

Deliver the requested outcome with evidence a teammate can inspect. Command success, current source, and sufficient proof are separate judgments.

## Establish the contract

Identify observable success, important regressions, constraints, and unresolved facts before implementation. Turn consequential claims into disprovable obligations. Trace the actual behavior through its execution and validation gates; a prerequisite that exists but is invalid must not enable an action or promise readiness.

For complex or long-running work, use [complex tasks](references/complex-tasks.md) to preserve dependencies, authority, blockers, review provenance, and recovery state. Use [harness guidance](references/harnesses.md) when delegating across Codex, Claude Code, or T3 Code. Use the lightest adequate process: **Quick** for clear, reversible local edits; **Standard** for ordinary bugs, features, and implementation-guiding research; **Critical** for consequential trust, money, destructive data, migration, or broad product changes. Use [mode examples](references/modes.md) and [task profiles](references/task-profiles.md) when the proof scope needs clarification. Explain the proof plan briefly. Preserve scope and existing authorization; continue discovery, implementation, repair, and verification autonomously. ## Build and challenge

Choose a small useful change that fits repository conventions. For bugs, reproduce the failure, then verify the fix. Exercise important boundaries through public behavior; mocks establish only the behavior they retain. If a claim depends on persistence or an external contract, run that boundary or mark the claim partial.

Use independent review for Critical work, consequential unresolved assumptions, changed trust/persistence/service contracts, surprising proof failures, or failures that are difficult to detect or undo. A reversible local mapping can use focused checks when it changes no such boundary; record why. Give the reviewer a narrow counterexample question and raw evidence. Critical work needs separate test-design and adversarial-review roles. Obtain independent proof design before implementation; review the resulting change adversarially afterward. Retain reviewer origin, scope, findings, and a resolvable reference; never invent independence. If required review is unavailable, disclose the gap. External model calls need authorization covering cost and data exposure.

Prefer one clear owner per rule, direct code, and abstractions justified by current needs. Remove unused scaffolding. Tests should have small readable setup, literal failure messages, and cases that could reject the claim. Avoid duplicated coverage and mocks that erase the boundary being tested.

## Verify and finish

Rerun affected proof after relevant code, test, or environment changes. Reuse current sufficient evidence; do not repeat passing checks solely for ceremony. Resolve failures before expanding the test scope.

Keep read-only requests read-only unless artifact creation is authorized. Required missing proof stays partial; optional exclusions remain visible with reasons.
